title: Verifying Rust Implementation of Page Tables in a Software Enclave Hypervisor
problem: Software enclave hypervisors implemented in Rust may contain semantic errors in page table configurations that break spatial isolation guarantees, even though Rust prevents memory safety bugs. Existing approaches rely on memory safety without verifying that page table management correctly enforces isolation between trust domains.
motivation: Spatial isolation is critical for TEE reliability and security in cloud computing, and configuration-level errors in memory subsystems can undermine the security properties of the entire system.
method: The approach uses formal verification—mathematically proving that code behaves as intended—to check Rust-based page table implementations (the data structures controlling which programs can access which memory locations) in software enclave hypervisors (software that creates isolated execution sandboxes). It verifies that page tables correctly enforce isolation boundaries between different trust domains so they cannot access each other's memory. Unlike Rust's built-in memory safety checks that prevent crashes, this detects logic errors in how isolation rules are written.
key_novelty: Using formal verification to detect logic errors in page table implementations that violate isolation, catching problems that Rust's memory safety guarantees alone cannot find.
contributions: Formal verification framework for page table implementations in software TEEs
Case study demonstrating verification of Rust hypervisor page table code
Methodology for detecting configuration-level isolation errors
Techniques to verify spatial isolation properties beyond memory safety guarantees

metrics.other: isolation properties verified, semantic correctness demonstrated

limitations: Abstract does not discuss verification scalability, performance overhead, or coverage completeness for large codebases.
